Scripted Wikimedia image downloads (generic UA) got HTTP 429; the Commons API itself works. On 2026-11-18 the user approved fetching the stop photos through their Chrome (Claude in Chrome: navigate to the upload.wikimedia.org file, fetch → blob → `<a download>`), and they clicked Chrome's "allow multiple downloads" prompt themselves.

**Why:** spoofing a browser UA in a script was refused as unauthorized; the user's real browser at human pace is fine.
**How to apply:** still ask before each new download batch (names, source, size). Use upload.wikimedia.org paths (thumbs live under /thumb/ there too). Move the files out of ~/Downloads into the scratchpad afterwards. Open follow-ups: SLK photo candidate and ghost tracing, see CLAUDE.md Open.

- **The exhibit:** The car was part of the museum's "Youngtimer" special exhibition and its "Close-up" series. It was in Collection Room 5 and was scheduled to be on display until 2 November 2025. Nine other classic cars from the '90s and '00s were shown alongside it.

- **The roof:** Coverage of the display highlights the vario-roof. One source describes it as a steel folding hardtop that turned the coupé into a convertible at the press of a button. Another calls it an electro-hydraulic folding roof made of steel, which the museum's press material called a stroke of engineering genius.
- **Background:** The roof was first shown on the SLK II concept at the 1994 Paris Motor Show. The production car went on sale in Europe two years later, in 1997 in the US.

For a current view of the museum's exhibits, check the museum's own website. The search results did not include one.

I couldn't find a museum photo of the SLK that we're free to use. Instead, the SLK stop now has a public-domain street photo of a 1997–2000 SLK, with a fitted camera and an outline traced from it.

**What I searched**
- **Commons:** I went through the Mercedes-Benz Museum categories (177 categories, about 1,960 files) and every file in the R170 category. None shows an SLK in the museum. The only "museum" SLK on Commons is at the Haynes Motor Museum in England. A 2011 Essen show car turned out to be the SLK owners' club stand.
- **Flickr:** the museum showed a yellow SLK 230 in its 2025 "Youngtimer" exhibition, but the photos of it there are all rights reserved. Filtered to Creative Commons, the results only show the later R172 SLK, at other venues.

**What I added**
- **Photo:** `stops/slk/photo.jpg` is "1st Mercedes-Benz SLK.jpg" by IFCAR (public domain), with the roof closed, seen from the front left, scaled to 1200 × 662. Following the SLS stop, the caption, note, credit and the "not taken in the museum" line say where it was taken. It replaces the old, unused photo of an SLK rebuilt with a 300 SL-style body.
- **Camera fit:** `tools/photo-fits/slk.json`, within 9.6 px on average. It rests on the two near wheels plus assumed positions for the headlamps, star and plate. I left the focal length free: the photo is a long zoom, about 11.6 m away.
- **Outline:** traced from the photo (`tools/profile-traces/slk.json`). The car's tail is cut off by the photo's edge, so the rear end comes from the data-sheet length.
- **Text:** the Hungarian file is updated to match, and CLAUDE.md's open list and my memory note are updated.

**Checked:** `npm test` passes (229 tests). Screenshots of the stop show no page errors at 55–58 fps. On the photo, the wheels, body side and the roof's moving panels line up with the car. I didn't run `npm run e2e`.

**Still rough:** the windscreen's edge sits about 35 px behind the near windscreen pillar's top in the photo. Lining them up would mean tilting the windscreen forward in the 3D model, so I left it.

Nothing is committed. If the museum's yellow SLK ever turns up under a free licence, swapping it in means a new photo plus a new camera fit.

Sources:
- [SLK 230 Kompressor in the Mercedes-Benz Museum's "Youngtimer" exhibition](https://emobilityplus.com/2025/05/24/slk-230-kompressor-shines-in-mercedes-benz-museums-youngtimer-exhibition/amp/)
- [File:1st Mercedes-Benz SLK.jpg (Commons)](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1st_Mercedes-Benz_SLK.jpg)
